You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Can the source mug be identified and tracked in the edited image well enough to judge its position relative to the headphones?
node.criteria: Pass only if the source mug can be matched to an edited object using visible identity or continuity cues, and that same object's position relative to the headphones can be judged. Fail if clear evidence shows the source mug is absent or unchanged and no matching moved mug is present. Unknown if blur, occlusion, or ambiguity prevents reliable matching or position judgment. Do not count a different mug as the source mug merely because it is visible.
node.binding: Compare source and edited images. Anchor the target to the single blue mug left of the headphones in the source; inspect the blurred blue remnant and any edited mugs for evidence of continuity. Record which edited object, if any, matches the source mug and why. This is evidence availability, not fulfillment.

node_traces.evidence: The source target is the single light-blue mug left of the headphones. In the edited image, a blurred blue remnant remains at the far left, while the visible mugs are white and lack clear identity cues linking either to the source mug. The remnant and mugs do not establish which edited object, if any, is the source mug, so its position relative to the headphones cannot be judged reliably.

The source target is the light-blue mug left of the headphones. In the edited image, a blurred blue remnant remains at the former left position, while two distinct mugs are visible: a small pale mug near the left headphone and a pale mug on the far right. The remnant and visible mugs provide enough continuity/context to identify a likely moved mug and judge its position relative to the headphones, though the exact match is ambiguous because the edited mugs differ visibly from the source mug.

The source target is the light-blue mug left of the headphones. In the edited image, a blurred blue remnant remains at the former left position, while two distinct mugs are visible: a small pale mug near the left headphone and a pale mug on the far right. The remnant and visible mugs provide enough continuity/identity context to track the source mug and judge its position relative to the headphones, though the exact match among the edited mugs is ambiguous.

The source target is the distinctive light-blue mug with a handle, left of the headphones. In the edited image, a blurred blue remnant remains at the far left, while two smaller mugs appear: a white mug near the left side of the headphones and a white mug to their right. The remnant and mugs do not provide reliable visible identity or continuity cues to match the original blue mug to either edited mug, so the source mug's position relative to the headphones cannot be judged reliably.

The source target is the single light-blue mug left of the headphones. In the edited image, a blurred blue remnant remains at the far left, while two distinct white mugs appear: one near the left headphone earcup and one to the right of the headphones. The blur and lack of clear identity/continuity cues make it ambiguous which, if either, is the source mug, so the source mug cannot be reliably matched to an edited object for judging its position.

s2: The binding is too compressed and omits the key s1 continuity evidence, so the node repeatedly defaults to unknown despite high confidence. Make the typed binding explicitly consume s1’s source-mug identity/continuity evidence and require a concrete comparison of candidate edited objects using visible attributes and spatial/context cues; distinguish a plausible match from an unresolvable one, without assuming the rightmost mug is the source mug. Here the source is a distinctive large light-blue mug left of the headphones; the edit shows a blurred blue form at far left and two smaller white mugs, so identity is genuinely ambiguous, not a transport or schema failure. Preserve unknown when continuity cannot be established, but have the node separately assess any evidenced displacement/progress of the tracked mug and report the basis, rather than treating uncertain final identity as proof that no progress occurred. The repeated identical unknown traces indicate a binding/evidence-routing bottleneck; confidence alone does not resolve it. Keep completion tied to verified same-mug placement right of the headphones, and do not force the aggregate reference label into this node as atomic ground truth.
